Q: How to loop a function and save the outputs of each run as independent objects? A:

Use Map and assign the result to list L and then L$mpg etc can get individual components. Alternately use list2env to place the components of L into the global environment. Normally using a list is preferable to having loose objects in the global environment.

# 1
library(dplyr)
 
calculate_summary <- function(var) {
  mtcars %>% 
    dplyr::group_by(cyl, vs) %>% 
    dplyr::summarise(
      N = length(.data[[var]]),
      mean = mean(.data[[var]]),
      sd   = sd(.data[[var]]),
      se   = sd / sqrt(N),
      .groups = "drop")
}
 
L <- Map(calculate_summary, c("mpg", "qsec"))
L$mpg
## # A tibble: 5 × 6
##     cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2     4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3     6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4     6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5     8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

or


# 2
list2env(L, globalenv())
<environment: R_GlobalEnv>

mpg
## # A tibble: 5 × 6
##     cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1     4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2     4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3     6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4     6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5     8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

Another approach is to create a single data frame and then filter it:

# 3
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)

DF <- map_dfr(set_names(c("mpg", "qsec")), calculate_summary, .id = "group")
filter(DF, group == "mpg")
## # A tibble: 5 × 7
##   group   cyl    vs     N  mean     sd     se
##   <chr> <dbl> <dbl> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>  <dbl>
## 1 mpg       4     0     1  26   NA     NA    
## 2 mpg       4     1    10  26.7  4.75   1.50 
## 3 mpg       6     0     3  20.6  0.751  0.433
## 4 mpg       6     1     4  19.1  1.63   0.816
## 5 mpg       8     0    14  15.1  2.56   0.684

If the last approach is of interest note that the dlookr package's describe function works with group_by eliminating calculate_summary.

# 4
library(dlookr)
library(dplyr)

DF2 <- mtcars %>%
  group_by(cyl, vs) %>%
  describe(mpg, qsec, statistics = c("mean", "sd", "se_mean"))

filter(DF2, described_variables == "mpg")
## # A tibble: 5 × 8
##   described_variables   cyl    vs     n    na  mean     sd se_mean
##   <chr>               <dbl> <dbl> <int> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1 mpg                     4     0     1     0  26   NA      NA    
## 2 mpg                     4     1    10     0  26.7  4.75    1.50 
## 3 mpg                     6     0     3     0  20.6  0.751   0.433
## 4 mpg                     6     1     4     0  19.1  1.63    0.816
## 5 mpg                     8     0    14     0  15.1  2.56    0.684

or to produce a list without calculate_summary add a split at the end:

# 5
library(dlookr)
library(dplyr)

L2 <- mtcars %>% 
  group_by(cyl, vs) %>%
  describe(mpg, qsec, statistics = c("mean", "sd", "se_mean")) %>%
  { split(.[-1], .[[1]]) }
L2$mpg
## # A tibble: 5 × 7
##     cyl    vs     n    na  mean     sd se_mean
##   <dbl> <dbl> <int> <int> <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>
## 1     4     0     1     0  26   NA      NA    
## 2     4     1    10     0  26.7  4.75    1.50 
## 3     6     0     3     0  20.6  0.751   0.433
## 4     6     1     4     0  19.1  1.63    0.816
## 5     8     0    14     0  15.1  2.56    0.684

Note that describe automatically excludes non-numeric variables so we can describe all numeric non-grouping columns like this or add split at the end to get a list.

# 6
group <- c("cyl", "vs")
DF3 <- mtcars %>%
  group_by(across(all_of(group), as.character)) %>%
  describe(statistics = c("mean", "sd", "se_mean"))
L3 <- DF3 %>% { split(.[-1], .[[1]]) }

Q: What is the difference between .one() and .scalar() A:

scalar() returns a Python scalar value, or None if no rows remain.

one() returns the first row from the result

So the difference is a Python value vs a SqlAlchemy Row object

Docs

https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Result.one https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/core/connections.html#sqlalchemy.engine.Result.scalar

Q: Intermittent 403 Forbidden client error response status code when scraping with Selenium A:

The 45–60 second recovery window makes rate limiting or an IP-based temporary block more likely than the User-Agent itself. I’d first remove the old Chrome 60 User-Agent override and use a current, matching browser version.

I’d also avoid immediately adding random User-Agents or clearing cookies, since that can create more inconsistencies. Instead, log the response body and headers around the first 403 and compare them with a normal response. If the block consistently clears after roughly a minute, reduce the request rate and use increasing backoff rather than always sleeping for exactly 60 seconds.

If the workload genuinely needs more throughput, distributing requests across multiple IPs can help with an IP-based limit. For example, I’ve used SquidProxies datacenter proxies for less restrictive scraping workloads, while residential proxies are generally a better fit when the target is particularly sensitive to datacenter IP reputation. I would keep the same proxy attached to a browser session rather than changing the IP on every request.

Also make sure the 403 is actually coming from the server/API rather than Selenium detecting a rendered block page. Selenium itself doesn't normally expose HTTP response status codes for every navigation, so checking the response body/network traffic can help distinguish a real 403 from a page that simply looks like one.

The key thing I'd investigate first is whether the 403 correlates with request count per IP. If it does, slowing the request rate or distributing the workload across a small number of stable IPs is more appropriate than trying to disguise the browser with an unusual User-Agent.

Q: SSL certificate error for IE users only A:

I found a work around for this issue. It is necessary to run https proxy which will accept certificate for Internet Explorer. I use a Python HTTP/HTTPS Proxy proxpy. You should point to required certificate file in core.py DEFAULT_CERT_FILE = "./cert/ncerts/proxpy.pem". So you need to use proxy settings in Internet Explorer. It is 127.0.0.1:8080 for ProxyPy by default.
